title: Writing: A holiday email
goal: Write a holiday email using the present perfect, the past simple and going to, with no, a little / a few, too much / too many and here / there.
goal_it: Scrivere l'email di una vacanza con present perfect, past simple e going to, usando no, a little / a few, too much / too many e here / there.

steps.title: Today: writing a holiday email
steps.title_it: Oggi: scrivere l'email di una vacanza
en: Today you write an email to a friend from a holiday, real or imaginary. You tell what you have done so far, what happened on one special day, and what you are going to do next.

You use three tenses together: the present perfect for experiences and news, the past simple to tell a finished day, and going to for plans. In the Language boost you also learn no, a little / a few, too much / too many, too + adjective, and here / there / over there.
it: Oggi scrivi un'email a un amico da una vacanza, vera o immaginaria. Racconti che cosa hai fatto finora, che cosa è successo in un giorno speciale e che cosa farai dopo.

Usi insieme tre tempi: il present perfect per esperienze e novità, il past simple per raccontare una giornata finita e going to per i progetti. Nel Language boost impari anche no, a little / a few, too much / too many, too + aggettivo e here / there / over there.

steps.title: Words for a holiday email
steps.title_it: Parole per l'email di una vacanza
en: Learn these ten words and expressions. They are in your flashcards too.
it: Impara queste dieci parole ed espressioni. Le trovi anche nelle flashcard.

steps.title: Model email
en: Greetings from Lisbon! I have been here for four days and I have already seen a lot. Yesterday we went up to the castle and took lots of photos. I have never eaten so many custard tarts in my life!

The only problem is the trams. There are too many tourists and the queue is too long, so we haven't tried the famous yellow tram yet. Tomorrow we are going to visit Sintra, and I'd like to see the palace there. Write soon!
it: Saluti da Lisbona! Sono qui da quattro giorni e ho già visto molto. Ieri siamo saliti al castello e abbiamo fatto un sacco di foto. Non ho mai mangiato così tanti pasticcini alla crema in vita mia!

L'unico problema sono i tram. Ci sono troppi turisti e la coda è troppo lunga, quindi non abbiamo ancora provato il famoso tram giallo. Domani visiteremo Sintra e mi piacerebbe vedere il palazzo. Scrivimi presto!

examples.en: I have been here for four days. (present perfect: news up to now)
examples.it: Sono qui da quattro giorni. (present perfect: novità fino a ora)

examples.en: Yesterday we went up to the castle. (past simple: finished day)
examples.it: Ieri siamo saliti al castello. (past simple: giorno finito)

examples.en: Tomorrow we are going to visit Sintra. (going to: plan)

steps.title: Language boost 1: quantifiers
en: no = not any, but stronger. The verb stays positive: There is no hot water. Use a little with uncountable nouns and a few with countable plural nouns: a little money, a few friends.
too much (uncountable) and too many (countable) mean more than you want: too much traffic, too many tourists. With an adjective use only too: The room is too small.
it: no = not any, ma più forte. Il verbo resta positivo: There is no hot water. A little si usa con gli uncountable e a few con i countable plurali: a little money, a few friends.
Too much (uncountable) e too many (countable) indicano più di quanto si vuole: too much traffic, too many tourists. Con un aggettivo si usa solo too: The room is too small.

steps.title: Language boost 2: here, there, over there
steps.title_it: Language boost 2: here, there, over there
en: here = near me. there = not near me, but not very far. over there = far from both of us, you point with your hand.
Examples: Come here, please. I left my bag there. The station is over there, behind the church.
it: here = vicino a me. there = non vicino a me, ma non molto lontano. over there = lontano da entrambi, lo indichi con la mano.
Esempi: Come here, please. I left my bag there. The station is over there, behind the church.

steps.title: Checklist before you write
en: Use this list to check every sentence, then read your text again.
it: Usa questa lista per controllare ogni frase, poi rileggi il testo.

head: Check
Example
rows: Present perfect: have/has + past participle, no finished time
I have already seen the castle.
Never with a positive verb, ever only in questions
I have never been to Rome. Have you ever been there?
Finished time (yesterday, last night): past simple
Yesterday we went to the beach.
Past simple negative and question: didn't / did + base verb
We didn't buy anything. Did you like it?
Plans: going to + base verb; wishes: would like to
We are going to take a boat. I'd like to swim.
Too much with uncountable, too many with countable plural
Too much noise, too many tourists.
First, then, after that. Hi Sara, Love, Anna

steps.q: Hi Sara! I ___ in Lisbon for four days now.
steps.q_it: Ciao Sara! Sono a Lisbona da quattro giorni ormai.
steps.why: For four days up to now: present perfect (have been). 'Am' ignores the duration, 'was' means it is finished.
steps.why_it: For four days fino a ora: present perfect (have been). 'Am' ignora la durata, 'was' indica che è finito.

steps.q: I have already ___ the castle. (see)
steps.q_it: Ho già visto il castello.
steps.why: Already goes with the present perfect: have + seen.
steps.why_it: Already va con il present perfect: have + seen.

steps.q: We ___ to the beach yesterday.
steps.q_it: Ieri siamo andati in spiaggia.
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time, so we use the past simple: went.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un tempo finito, quindi past simple: went.

steps.q: I have never ___ so much fish! (eat)
steps.q_it: Non ho mai mangiato così tanto pesce!
steps.why: Never goes with the present perfect and a positive verb: have never eaten.
steps.why_it: Never va con il present perfect e verbo positivo: have never eaten.

steps.q: Have you ever ___ a Portuguese custard tart? (try)
steps.q_it: Hai mai provato un pasticcino alla crema portoghese?
steps.why: Ever in a question about experience: Have you ever + past participle.
steps.why_it: Ever in una domanda sull'esperienza: Have you ever + participio passato.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: Last night we went to a small restaurant
steps.why: Last night is finished, so the verb is in the past simple: went.
steps.why_it: Last night è finito, quindi il verbo è al past simple: went.

steps.q: Tomorrow we ___ visit the palace.
steps.q_it: Domani visiteremo il palazzo.
steps.why: A plan already decided: be going to + base verb.
steps.why_it: Un progetto già deciso: be going to + verbo base.

steps.q: I'd like ___ the old town again. (visit)
steps.q_it: Mi piacerebbe visitare di nuovo la città vecchia.
steps.why: Would like is followed by to + base verb.
steps.why_it: Would like è seguito da to + verbo base.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: We are going to take the train to Sintra
steps.why: Plan: subject + are going to + base verb.
steps.why_it: Progetto: soggetto + are going to + verbo base.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct in an email?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta in un'email?
options: I have visited the museum yesterday.
I have been visiting the museum yesterday.
steps.why: Yesterday needs the past simple. The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time.
steps.why_it: Yesterday vuole il past simple. Il present perfect non si usa con un tempo finito.

steps.q: There is ___ time, so we must hurry.
steps.q_it: Non c'è tempo, quindi dobbiamo sbrigarci.
steps.why: Time is uncountable. No time means not any time. Many and a few are for countable plural nouns.
steps.why_it: Time è uncountable. No time significa nessun tempo. Many e a few sono per i countable plurali.

steps.q: I've only got ___ money left, so I can't buy a souvenir. (a little / a few)
steps.q_it: Mi sono rimasti pochi soldi, quindi non posso comprare un souvenir.
steps.why: Money is uncountable: a little.
steps.why_it: Money è uncountable: a little.

steps.q: We met ___ nice people on the tour. (a little / a few)
steps.q_it: Abbiamo conosciuto alcune persone simpatiche durante il tour.
steps.why: People is countable plural: a few.
steps.why_it: People è countable plurale: a few.

steps.q: The hotel is cheap, but the room is ___ small.
steps.q_it: L'hotel è economico, ma la camera è troppo piccola.
steps.why: Before an adjective we use only too.
steps.why_it: Davanti a un aggettivo si usa solo too.

steps.q: There are ___ tourists in August, so I never go. (too much / too many)
steps.q_it: Ad agosto ci sono troppi turisti, quindi non vado mai.
steps.why: Tourists is countable plural: too many.
steps.why_it: Tourists è countable plurale: too many.

steps.q: I ate ___ ice cream and now I feel ill. (too much / too many)
steps.q_it: Ho mangiato troppo gelato e ora sto male.
steps.why: Ice cream is uncountable: too much.
steps.why_it: Ice cream è uncountable: too much.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: There is no hot water in our room
There's no hot water in our room
steps.why: No + noun with a positive verb: There is no hot water.
steps.why_it: No + nome con verbo positivo: There is no hot water.

steps.q: Which sentence is correct?
steps.q_it: Quale frase è corretta?
steps.why: English has only one negative: no with a positive verb. The double negation is a mistake.
steps.why_it: In inglese c'è una sola negazione: no con verbo positivo. La doppia negazione è un errore.

steps.q: Come ___, please. I'm next to the window and I want to show you the view. (here / there)
steps.q_it: Vieni qui, per favore. Sono vicino alla finestra e voglio farti vedere il panorama.
steps.why: Near the speaker: here.
steps.why_it: Vicino a chi parla: here.

steps.q: Look at the hill far away, ___. We are going there tomorrow.
steps.q_it: Guarda la collina lontana, laggiù. Domani andremo là.
steps.why: Far from both speakers and pointing: over there.
steps.why_it: Lontano da entrambi e indicando: over there.

steps.q: The bus stop is ___, on the other side of the road. (here / there / over there)
steps.q_it: La fermata dell'autobus è laggiù, dall'altra parte della strada.
steps.why: Far away, on the other side: over there.
steps.why_it: Lontano, dall'altra parte: over there.

steps.q: Put the words in order.
steps.q_it: Metti le parole in ordine.
answers: The museum is over there next to the bank
steps.why: Over there goes after the verb be, then the place.
steps.why_it: Over there va dopo il verbo be, poi il luogo.

steps.q: We arrived on Monday. We have been here ___ Monday. (for / since)
steps.q_it: Siamo arrivati lunedì. Siamo qui da lunedì.
steps.why: Monday is a starting point: since.
steps.why_it: Monday è un punto di partenza: since.

steps.q: I'm tired because I ___ all day. (walk)
steps.q_it: Sono stanco perché ho camminato tutto il giorno.
steps.why: Activity that lasted until now with a visible result: have been walking.
steps.why_it: Attività durata fino a ora con risultato visibile: have been walking.

steps.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
steps.q_it: Quale frase contiene un errore?
options: I have been to Paris twice.
I have never been there in winter.
I have seen the Eiffel Tower yesterday.
steps.why: Yesterday is a finished time, so you need the past simple: I saw the Eiffel Tower yesterday.
steps.why_it: Yesterday è un tempo finito, serve il past simple: I saw the Eiffel Tower yesterday.

steps.q: Choose the best sentence: 'The tickets cost a lot and I can't buy them.'
steps.q_it: Scegli la frase migliore.
options: The tickets are too much expensive.
The tickets are too many expensive.
The tickets are very much expensive.
steps.why: Too before an adjective, without much or many.
steps.why_it: Too davanti a un aggettivo, senza much né many.

steps.title: Your writing task
en: Write an email to a friend from a holiday (real or imaginary) in eight to ten sentences. Include: a greeting, one present perfect with already, never or ever, two past simple sentences about one day, one going to, one would like to, one quantifier (too much, too many, a little, a few or no) and here, there or over there once.
Write on paper or in your notes app. This app does not correct your text, so read it again with the checklist and check each sentence.
If you want, share your email with a friend from the class and compare.
it: Scrivi un'email a un amico da una vacanza (vera o immaginaria) in otto dieci frasi. Includi: un saluto, un present perfect con already, never o ever, due frasi al past simple su una giornata, un going to, un would like to, un quantificatore (too much, too many, a little, a few o no) e here, there o over there una volta.
Scrivi su carta o nell'app note. L'app non corregge il testo, quindi rileggilo con la checklist e controlla ogni frase.
Se vuoi, condividi l'email con un compagno del corso e confrontatela.

cards.ex: I have seen three museums so far.
There is a long queue at the castle.
The sea is lovely. Wish you were here!
We met a few nice people.
